decisions.choice: as their fathers forgot my name through Baal: the same sin as before
decisions.reason: In the days of the judges and of Ahab, Israel turned to Baal and forgot the LORD (Judges 3:7; 1 Kings 18:21; Hosea 2:15). The dream prophets lead the people the same way, even when they speak in the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: by worshiping Baal
decisions.reason: Readable says how Baal made them forget: they worshiped him.

decisions.choice: Verses 26-27 closed as separate sentences
alternatives: one question running across the verses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew question runs on from verse 26; Korean cannot leave a relative clause hanging after a verse marker, so each verse is closed as its own sentence, with verse 27 as a statement.

source.text: הַנָּבִ֞יא אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֤וֹ חֲלוֹם֙ יְסַפֵּ֣ר חֲל֔וֹם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר דְּבָרִי֙ אִתּ֔וֹ יְדַבֵּ֥ר דְּבָרִ֖י אֱמֶ֑ת מַה־לַתֶּ֥בֶן אֶת־הַבָּ֖ר נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The prophet who [is] with him a dream, let him recount a dream, and [he] who my word [is] with him, let him speak my word [in] faithfulness. What [is] to the straw with the grain? declares Yahweh.

en.L: The prophet who has a dream, let him recount a dream; and the one who has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, let him speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word faithfully. What [has] the straw [to do] with the grain? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Let the prophet who has a dream tell it as a dream, but let the one who has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: If a prophet has had a dream, let him say it is only a dream. But if someone has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message, let that person speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message faithfully. Straw is nothing like grain! says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: El profeta que tenga un sueño, que cuente un sueño; y el que tenga {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, que hable {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra con fidelidad. ¿Qué [tiene que ver] la paja con el trigo?, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: El profeta que tenga un sueño, que lo cuente como sueño; pero el que tenga {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, que hable {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra fielmente. ¿Qué tiene en común la paja con el trigo?, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Si un profeta ha tenido un sueño, que diga que solo es un sueño. Pero si alguien tiene {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensaje, que lo comunique fielmente. ¡La paja no se parece en nada al trigo!, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Le prophète qui a un songe, qu’il raconte un songe ; et celui qui a {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole, qu’il dise {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole fidèlement. Qu’[a de commun] la paille avec le blé ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Que le prophète qui a eu un rêve le raconte comme un rêve, mais que celui qui a {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole dise {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole fidèlement. Qu’y a-t-il de commun entre la paille et le blé ? déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Si un prophète a fait un rêve, qu’il dise que ce n’est qu’un rêve. Mais si quelqu’un a {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} message, qu’il le transmette fidèlement. La paille n’a rien à voir avec le blé ! dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nabii aliye na ndoto, na asimulie ndoto; na yule aliye na neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na alinene neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kwa uaminifu. Makapi yana nini na nafaka? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nabii aliye na ndoto na aisimulie kama ndoto tu, lakini yule aliye na neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} na alinene neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kwa uaminifu. Makapi yanafanana nini na nafaka? asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ikiwa nabii ameota ndoto, na aseme kwamba ni ndoto tu. Lakini ikiwa mtu ana ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, mtu huyo na autoe ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa uaminifu. Makapi si kitu ukiyalinganisha na nafaka! anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Nhà tiên tri nào có giấc mộng, hãy thuật lại giấc mộng; còn ai có lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, hãy trung tín nói lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Rơm rạ có liên quan gì đến lúa thóc? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Nhà tiên tri nào có giấc mộng, hãy kể đó là giấc mộng; nhưng ai có lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, hãy trung tín rao truyền lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Rơm rạ có gì chung với lúa thóc? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Nếu nhà tiên tri nào có giấc mộng, hãy nói rằng đó chỉ là giấc mộng. Nhưng ai có sứ điệp của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, người ấy hãy trung tín nói lại sứ điệp của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Rơm rạ chẳng giống gì lúa thóc! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 꿈을 꾼 예언자는 꿈을 이야기하고, 내 말을 받은 자는 내 말을 진실하게 전하여라. 짚이 곡식과 무슨 상관이 [있느냐]? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 꿈을 꾼 예언자는 그것을 꿈이라고 이야기하고, 내 말을 받은 사람은 내 말을 충실하게 전하여라. 짚과 곡식이 어떻게 같으냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 예언자가 꿈을 꾸었으면 그것이 꿈일 뿐이라고 말하게 하여라. 그러나 내 말을 받은 사람은 내 말을 충실하게 전하게 하여라. 짚은 곡식과 전혀 다르다! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

pt.L: O profeta que tem um sonho, que conte um sonho; e aquele que tem a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, que fale a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra com fidelidade. Que [tem] a palha [a ver] com o trigo? declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: O profeta que tem um sonho, que o conte como sonho; mas aquele que tem a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, que fale a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra com fidelidade. O que a palha tem em comum com o trigo? declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Se um profeta teve um sonho, que diga que é só um sonho. Mas, se alguém tem a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mensagem, que anuncie a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mensagem com fidelidade. A palha não tem nada a ver com o trigo! diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: let him recount a dream: let him call it a dream and nothing more
decisions.reason: God does not forbid telling dreams. He sets a dream beside his word: let a dream be told as a dream, and not passed off as the word of the LORD.

decisions.choice: faithfully: in truth, as it was given
decisions.reason: The word means truth and faithfulness. The prophet who has God's word must pass it on as he received it, adding nothing and leaving nothing out (26:2).

decisions.choice: straw and grain: the worthless set beside the real thing
decisions.reason: When grain was threshed, the straw and chaff were separated from the kernels (Psalm 1:4). The prophets' dreams are straw; God's word is the grain that feeds.

decisions.choice: Straw is nothing like grain!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

source.text: הֲל֨וֹא כֹ֧ה דְבָרִ֛י כָּאֵ֖שׁ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וּכְפַטִּ֖ישׁ יְפֹ֥צֵֽץ סָֽלַע׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not thus my word like fire, declares Yahweh, and like a hammer [that] shatters rock?

en.L: Is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word like this, like fire, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
en.B: Is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word like fire, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like a hammer that smashes rock to pieces?
en.R: My word is like fire, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is like a hammer that smashes rocks to pieces.

es.L: ¿No es así {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, como fuego, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y como martillo que quebranta la roca?
es.B: ¿No es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra como fuego, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, como un martillo que hace pedazos la roca?
es.R: Mi palabra es como fuego, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Es como un martillo que hace pedazos las rocas.

fr.L: Ma parole n’est-elle pas ainsi, comme un feu, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et comme un marteau qui brise le roc ?
fr.B: Ma parole n’est-elle pas comme un feu, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, comme un marteau qui fait voler le roc en éclats ?
fr.R: Ma parole est comme un feu, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Elle est comme un marteau qui fait éclater les rochers.

sw.L: Je, neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} si kama hivi, kama moto, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na kama nyundo ipasuayo mwamba?
sw.B: Je, neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} si kama moto, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kama nyundo ivunjayo mwamba vipande vipande?
sw.R: Neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} ni kama moto, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ni kama nyundo inayovunja miamba vipande vipande.

vi.L: Chẳng phải lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giống như vậy, như lửa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, và như búa đập vỡ đá sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như lửa sao, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, như búa đập đá vỡ tan sao?
vi.R: Lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như lửa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Lời ấy như chiếc búa đập đá vỡ tan.

ko.L: 내 말이 이와 같이 불 같지 않으냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 바위를 부수는 망치 같지 않으냐?
ko.B: 내 말은 불과 같지 않으냐? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 바위를 산산조각 내는 망치와 같지 않으냐?
ko.R: 내 말은 불과 같다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내 말은 바위를 산산조각 내는 망치와 같다.

pt.L: Não é assim a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra, como fogo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e como um martelo que despedaça a rocha?
pt.B: Não é a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra como fogo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, como um martelo que despedaça a rocha?
pt.R: A {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} palavra é como fogo, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Ela é como um martelo que despedaça as rochas.

decisions.choice: my word like fire: God's word burns and cannot be held back
decisions.reason: God told Jeremiah that his words in the prophet's mouth would be fire that burns up the people like wood (5:14), and Jeremiah felt it as a fire shut up in his bones (20:9). Unlike the prophets' dreams, it does what it says.

decisions.choice: a hammer that shatters rock: nothing can stand against it
decisions.reason: The verb means to break into pieces. God's word breaks down the hardest resistance.

decisions.choice: My word is like fire (a statement)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects the answer "yes", into a statement.

source.text: לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י עַל־הַנְּבִאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה מְגַנְּבֵ֣י דְבָרַ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֥ת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore look, I [am] against the prophets, declares Yahweh, stealing my words each from his neighbor.

en.L: Therefore look, I [am] against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who steal {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, each from {{gender:their|his}} neighbor.
en.B: So I am against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who steal {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words from one another.
en.R: So I am against these prophets, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They steal messages from each other and say they are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

es.L: Por tanto, he aquí, yo [estoy] contra los profetas, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que roban {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras cada uno a su prójimo.
es.B: Por eso yo estoy contra los profetas, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que se roban {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras unos a otros.
es.R: Por eso yo estoy contra estos profetas, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Se roban los mensajes unos a otros y dicen que son {{deity_pronoun:míos|Míos}}.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi voici, [je suis] contre les prophètes, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui volent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles, chacun à son prochain.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi je suis contre les prophètes, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui se volent {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles les uns aux autres.
fr.R: Alors je suis contre ces prophètes, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils se volent des messages les uns aux autres et prétendent qu’ils viennent de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] juu ya manabii, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wanaoiba maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kila mmoja kutoka kwa jirani yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni dhidi ya manabii, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wanaoibiana maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni dhidi ya manabii hawa, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanaibiana ujumbe na kusema kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

vi.L: Vì vậy, kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng các nhà tiên tri, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, là những kẻ ăn cắp lời Ta, người này của người kia.
vi.B: Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng các nhà tiên tri, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, là những kẻ ăn cắp lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} của nhau.
vi.R: Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng những nhà tiên tri này, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Chúng ăn cắp sứ điệp của nhau rồi bảo đó là sứ điệp của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러므로 보아라, 저마다 자기 이웃에게서 내 말을 훔치는 예언자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 서로 내 말을 훔치는 예언자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 이 예언자들을 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그들은 서로 남의 말을 훔쳐서 내 말이라고 한다.

pt.L: Portanto, eis que eu [estou] contra os profetas, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que roubam as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras, cada um do seu próximo.
pt.B: Por isso, eu estou contra os profetas, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que roubam as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras uns dos outros.
pt.R: Por isso, eu estou contra esses profetas, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Eles roubam mensagens uns dos outros e dizem que elas são {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}}.

decisions.choice: I am against: God sets himself as their enemy
decisions.reason: The phrase "look, I am against ..." announces that God will act against someone (21:13; 50:31; Ezekiel 13:8).

decisions.choice: steal my words: pass off borrowed words as God's
decisions.reason: Having no word of their own from God, they take phrases from one another, or from true prophets, and present them as a message from the LORD.

decisions.choice: and say they are mine
decisions.reason: Readable says what "steal my words" means (m2).

decisions.choice: "내가 치겠다" for "I am against"
decisions.reason: Korean says what God's being "against" them means (meaning decision m1), and puts the verb at the end of the sentence, after the description of the prophets.

source.text: הִנְנִ֥י עַל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הַלֹּקְחִ֣ים לְשׁוֹנָ֔ם וַֽיִּנְאֲמ֖וּ נְאֻֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] against the prophets, declares Yahweh, taking their tongue and declaring, [it is] a declaration.

en.L: Look, I [am] against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who take their own tongues and declare, "Declares [{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}]."
en.B: I am against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who speak with their own tongues and then announce, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} declares."
en.R: I am against these prophets, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They make up their own messages and then say, "This is a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: He aquí, yo [estoy] contra los profetas, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que toman su propia lengua y declaran: «Declara [{{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}]».
es.B: Yo estoy contra los profetas, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que hablan con su propia lengua y luego anuncian: «Afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.R: Yo estoy contra estos profetas, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Inventan sus propios mensajes y luego dicen: «Este es un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Voici, [je suis] contre les prophètes, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui prennent leur langue et déclarent : « Déclare [{{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}]. »
fr.B: Je suis contre les prophètes, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui parlent avec leur propre langue et proclament ensuite : « Déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Je suis contre ces prophètes, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils inventent leurs propres messages, puis ils disent : « C’est un message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] juu ya manabii, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wanaotumia ndimi zao wenyewe na kutamka, "Asema [{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}]."
sw.B: Mimi ni dhidi ya manabii, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wanaonena kwa ndimi zao wenyewe kisha kutangaza, "Asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Mimi ni dhidi ya manabii hawa, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanabuni ujumbe wao wenyewe kisha wanasema, "Huu ni ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng các nhà tiên tri, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, là những kẻ dùng lưỡi mình mà nói: "[{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}] phán vậy."
vi.B: Ta nghịch cùng các nhà tiên tri, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, là những kẻ dùng lưỡi mình mà nói rồi tuyên bố: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy."
vi.R: Ta nghịch cùng những nhà tiên tri này, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Chúng tự bịa ra sứ điệp rồi nói: "Đây là sứ điệp từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

ko.L: 보아라, 자기 혀를 놀려 "[{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의] 선언이다." 하고 선언하는 예언자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 제멋대로 혀를 놀려 말하고는 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신다." 하고 선언하는 예언자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 이 예언자들을 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그들은 자기들이 말을 지어내 놓고는 "이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 말씀이다." 하고 말한다.

pt.L: Eis que eu [estou] contra os profetas, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que tomam a sua [própria] língua e declaram: "Declara [{{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}]."
pt.B: Eu estou contra os profetas, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, que falam com a sua própria língua e depois anunciam: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} declara."
pt.R: Eu estou contra esses profetas, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Eles inventam as suas próprias mensagens e depois dizem: "Esta é uma mensagem {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}."

decisions.choice: declare, "Declares": a play on the prophets' formula
decisions.reason: The noun "declaration" is the word in the formula "declares the LORD", which closes many of God's sayings in this chapter. The prophets use only their own tongues and then add the formula, borrowing God's authority for their own words.

decisions.choice: Declares [the LORD] (Literal); The LORD declares (Balanced); This is a message from the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the word of the formula alone. English supplies "the LORD" so that the reader can recognize the formula.

decisions.choice: declaran: «Declara» (Literal); anuncian: «Afirma el SEÑOR» (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The play on the prophets' formula (meaning decision m1) uses each level's own Spanish wording of *neʾum YHWH*, so the reader hears the formula the false prophets borrow.

decisions.choice: "Asema [BWANA]" / "Asema BWANA"
decisions.reason: The false prophets borrow the formula itself, so Literal and Balanced quote the settled Swahili "asema BWANA" (meaning decision m1); Readable says what they claim.

decisions.choice: "[CHÚA] phán vậy" / "CHÚA phán vậy"
decisions.reason: The prophets borrow the very formula God uses ("phán vậy"), so Literal and Balanced quote it in the form that closes God's own words, to keep the play of meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: "선언하다 ... 선언이다" (L); "말씀하신다" in their mouths (B)
decisions.reason: The prophets misuse the formula *neʾum YHWH* (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the verb and noun of the same root, as the Hebrew does; in the prophets' own mouths the formula takes the honorific, since they claim to speak about God.

source.text: הִ֠נְנִי עַֽל־נִבְּאֵ֞י חֲלֹמ֥וֹת שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיְסַפְּרוּם֙ וַיַּתְע֣וּ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י בְּשִׁקְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְפַחֲזוּתָ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֨י לֹֽא־שְׁלַחְתִּ֜ים וְלֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֗ים וְהוֹעֵ֛יל לֹֽא־יוֹעִ֥ילוּ לָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] against those prophesying dreams of falsehood, declares Yahweh, and they recount them and lead astray my people by their falsehoods and by their recklessness, and I not sent them and not commanded them, and benefit not they will benefit this people, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Look, I [am] against those who prophesy false dreams, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and recount them and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people astray by their falsehoods and by their recklessness, though I did not send them and did not command them; and they will not benefit this people at all, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I am against those who prophesy false dreams, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They tell them and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people astray with their lies and their reckless boasting, though I did not send them or give them any command. They do this people no good at all, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I am against the prophets who tell false dreams, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They tell these dreams and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people the wrong way with their lies and their wild boasting. But I did not send them or give them orders. They do not help these people at all, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: He aquí, yo [estoy] contra los que profetizan sueños de mentira, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y los cuentan y hacen errar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo con sus mentiras y con su temeridad, aunque yo no los envié ni les mandé; y no traerán provecho alguno a este pueblo, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Yo estoy contra los que profetizan sueños falsos, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Los cuentan y extravían a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo con sus mentiras y sus fanfarronadas temerarias, aunque yo no los envié ni les di ninguna orden. No le hacen ningún bien a este pueblo, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Yo estoy contra los profetas que cuentan sueños falsos, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Cuentan esos sueños y llevan a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo por mal camino con sus mentiras y sus alardes descabellados. Pero yo no los envié ni les di órdenes. No ayudan en nada a este pueblo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Voici, [je suis] contre ceux qui prophétisent des songes de mensonge, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui les racontent et égarent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple par leurs mensonges et par leur vantardise, alors que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ne les ai pas envoyés et ne leur ai rien ordonné ; et ils ne sont d’aucune utilité à ce peuple, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je suis contre ceux qui prophétisent des rêves mensongers, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils les racontent et égarent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple par leurs mensonges et leurs vantardises insensées, alors que je ne les ai pas envoyés et que je ne leur ai donné aucun ordre. Ils ne sont d’aucune utilité à ce peuple, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je suis contre les prophètes qui racontent des rêves mensongers, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils racontent ces rêves et conduisent {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple sur le mauvais chemin par leurs mensonges et leurs vantardises folles. Mais je ne les ai pas envoyés et je ne leur ai donné aucun ordre. Ils n’aident pas du tout ce peuple, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Tazama, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] juu yao wanaotabiri ndoto za uongo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na kuzisimulia na kuwapotosha watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa uongo wao na kwa majivuno yao ya kipuuzi, ingawa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sikuwatuma wala sikuwaamuru; wala hawatawafaidia watu hawa kamwe, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mimi ni dhidi ya wale wanaotabiri ndoto za uongo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanazisimulia na kuwapotosha watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa uongo wao na majivuno yao ya kizembe, ingawa sikuwatuma wala sikuwapa amri yoyote. Hawawafaidii watu hawa hata kidogo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mimi ni dhidi ya manabii wanaosimulia ndoto za uongo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanasimulia ndoto hizo na kuwaongoza watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika njia mbaya kwa uongo wao na majivuno yao ya kipumbavu. Lakini sikuwatuma wala sikuwapa maagizo. Hawawasaidii watu hawa hata kidogo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghịch cùng những kẻ nói tiên tri bằng những giấc mộng giả dối, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, chúng thuật lại các giấc mộng ấy và làm cho dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lầm lạc bởi sự giả dối và sự khoác lác liều lĩnh của chúng, dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không sai chúng và không truyền lệnh cho chúng; và chúng chẳng làm ích lợi gì cho dân này cả, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta nghịch cùng những kẻ nói tiên tri bằng những giấc mộng giả dối, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy. Chúng kể lại các giấc mộng ấy và dẫn dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi lạc bằng những lời dối trá và khoác lác liều lĩnh, dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng hề sai chúng hay truyền lệnh gì cho chúng. Chúng chẳng đem lại ích lợi gì cho dân này cả, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta nghịch cùng những nhà tiên tri kể những giấc mộng giả dối, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Chúng kể những giấc mộng ấy và dẫn dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi sai đường bằng những lời dối trá và khoe khoang ngông cuồng. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không sai chúng, cũng không ra lệnh cho chúng. Chúng chẳng giúp ích gì cho dân này cả, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 보아라, 거짓 꿈을 예언하고 그것을 이야기하며 그들의 거짓말과 허풍으로 내 백성을 잘못된 길로 이끄는 자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 나는 그들을 보내지도 않았고 그들에게 명령하지도 않았다. 그들은 이 백성에게 조금도 유익을 주지 못할 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 거짓 꿈을 예언하는 자들을 내가 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그들은 그 꿈을 이야기하며 거짓말과 무모한 허풍으로 내 백성을 그릇된 길로 이끈다. 나는 그들을 보내지도 않았고 그들에게 아무것도 명령하지 않았다. 그들은 이 백성에게 아무 도움도 되지 않는다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 거짓 꿈 이야기를 하는 예언자들을 치겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그들은 그 꿈 이야기를 하면서 거짓말과 터무니없는 허풍으로 내 백성을 잘못된 길로 이끈다. 그러나 나는 그들을 보낸 적도 없고 그들에게 명령한 적도 없다. 그들은 이 백성에게 조금도 도움이 되지 않는다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

pt.L: Eis que eu [estou] contra os que profetizam sonhos mentirosos, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e os contam e desencaminham o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo com as suas mentiras e com a sua leviandade, embora eu não os tenha enviado nem lhes tenha dado ordem; e de nada servirão a este povo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Eu estou contra os que profetizam sonhos falsos, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Eles os contam e desviam o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo com as suas mentiras e a sua fanfarronice irresponsável, embora eu não os tenha enviado nem lhes tenha dado ordem alguma. Eles não fazem bem nenhum a este povo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Eu estou contra os profetas que contam sonhos falsos, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Eles contam esses sonhos e levam o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo pelo caminho errado com as suas mentiras e a sua fanfarronice. Mas eu não os enviei nem lhes dei ordens. Eles não ajudam este povo em nada, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: recklessness: wild, boastful talk
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root used of people who are reckless and undisciplined (Judges 9:4), and of prophets who are "reckless" (Zephaniah 3:4). Here it is the prophets' careless, swaggering talk.

decisions.choice: not benefit at all: the doubled verb for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, a Hebrew way of saying "not in the least". The same verb is used for idols that cannot help (2:8, 11; 16:19).

decisions.choice: reckless boasting (Balanced); wild boasting (Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrase brings out both sides of the word (m1).

source.text: וְכִי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ֩ הָעָ֨ם הַזֶּ֜ה אֽוֹ־הַנָּבִ֤יא אֽוֹ־כֹהֵן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַה־מַשָּׂ֖א יְהוָ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־מַה־מַשָּׂ֔א וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when asks you this people or the prophet or a priest, saying: what [is the] burden of Yahweh? then you will say to them: what burden? and I will cast you off, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And when this people or the prophet or a priest asks you, saying, "What [is] the burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" then you will say to them, "What burden? I will cast you off, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden?" you are to say to them, "What burden? I will throw you off, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: When these people, or a prophet or a priest, ask you, "What is {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden? What message does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} have for us?" tell them, "What burden? I will throw you away, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: Y cuando te pregunte este pueblo, o el profeta, o un sacerdote, diciendo: «¿Cuál [es] la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?», entonces les dirás: «¿Qué carga? {{plural_you:Los|Os}} arrojaré, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.B: Cuando este pueblo, o un profeta, o un sacerdote te pregunte: «¿Cuál es la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?», les dirás: «¿Qué carga? {{plural_you:Los|Os}} arrojaré lejos de mí, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».
es.R: Cuando esta gente, o un profeta, o un sacerdote te pregunte: «¿Cuál es la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? ¿Qué mensaje tiene {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para nosotros?», diles: «¿Qué carga? {{plural_you:Los|Os}} voy a tirar como una carga, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

decisions.choice: burden: both a heavy load and a message from God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to lift, to carry". It means a load that is carried, and it is also the usual title for a prophet's message (Isaiah 13:1; 15:1; Nahum 1:1), something "lifted up" by the voice, often a heavy word of judgment. Verses 33-40 play on both senses: the people ask mockingly for the LORD's latest "burden", and God answers that they themselves are a load he will throw off.

decisions.choice: "What burden?" (the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "What burden?" The same consonants, divided differently, read "You are the burden", and the Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate have that reading: "You are the burden, and I will cast you off." The Hebrew is kept; both readings say that the people, not God's word, are the weight God will throw down. This claim about the ancient versions is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: you: Jeremiah
decisions.reason: God speaks to the prophet, telling him how to answer those who ask for a "burden".

decisions.choice: cast off: let fall, abandon
decisions.reason: The verb means to let something fall or to leave it lying, as a load is thrown down (7:29; 12:7). It fits the picture of the burden.

decisions.choice: burden at every level; Readable adds "What message does he have for us?"
decisions.reason: Only a word that means both a load and a message keeps the play of verses 33-40, and "burden" is kept in every verse so that the play can be followed. Readable adds a question that says what the people mean by it.

decisions.choice: carga, at every level
decisions.reason: In 23:33-40 *massa* is "carga" at every level, as the terms note sets, to keep the wordplay between a heavy load and a message from God (meaning decision m1). Readable adds "¿Qué mensaje tiene él para nosotros?" so the second sense is clear.

decisions.choice: mzigo
decisions.reason: In 23:33-40 *massa* is "mzigo" (a load) at every level, so the wordplay on the burden and the message can be followed, as the terms note sets; elsewhere it is "unabii" or "ujumbe". Readable adds the question about a message, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "fardeau" at every level in verses 33-40
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: only a word that means both a load and a message keeps the play of these verses, and "fardeau" is kept in every verse so the reader can follow it; Readable adds "Quel message ... ?" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "gánh nặng" (burden) at every level in verses 33-40
decisions.reason: As the terms note settles, "massa" is "gánh nặng" here, not the usual "sấm ngôn" / "sứ điệp", so that the play between a message from God and a heavy load is kept; Readable adds a plain question, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "짐" for *massa* at every level in 23:33-40
decisions.reason: As the terms note: elsewhere *massa* is "신탁", but here the wordplay between a message and a heavy load is the point (meaning decision m1), so "짐" stands at every level; Readable adds the people's meaning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The people ask in 해라체 ("무엇이냐?")
decisions.reason: The question is mocking (meaning decision m1), so the people do not speak to Jeremiah politely.

decisions.choice: o fardo, at every level and through verses 33-40
decisions.reason: The word means both a load to be carried and a message from God (m1), and the play of these verses rests on the load: God will throw the people off like a load (m4). Portuguese has no one word for both, so it keeps "fardo", the load, in every verse, as the English keeps "burden", and Readable says the second sense once, as the English Readable does. Isaiah's heading word "oráculo" would lose the play.

en.L: But "the burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}" you shall not mention again, for the burden will be to each one {{gender:their|his}} own word; and you have twisted the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, our God.
en.B: But you must never again speak of "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," because each person's own word will become their burden, and you twist the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, our God.
en.R: But you must stop saying "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." Each person's own words will become a heavy burden for them. You have twisted the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, our God.

es.L: Pero «la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}» no la {{plural_you:mencionarán|mencionaréis}} más, porque la carga será para cada uno su propia palabra; y {{plural_you:ustedes han|vosotros habéis}} torcido las palabras del Dios vivo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, nuestro Dios.
es.B: Pero nunca más {{plural_you:hablen|habléis}} de «la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}», porque la palabra de cada uno se convertirá en su propia carga, y {{plural_you:ustedes tuercen|vosotros torcéis}} las palabras del Dios vivo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, nuestro Dios.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} de decir «la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}». Las propias palabras de cada uno se convertirán en una carga pesada para él. {{plural_you:Ustedes han|Vosotros habéis}} torcido las palabras del Dios vivo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, nuestro Dios.

fr.L: Mais « le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », vous ne le mentionnerez plus, car le fardeau sera pour chacun sa propre parole ; et vous avez déformé les paroles du Dieu vivant, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, notre Dieu.
fr.B: Mais vous ne parlerez plus jamais du « fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », car la parole de chacun deviendra son propre fardeau, et vous déformez les paroles du Dieu vivant, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, notre Dieu.
fr.R: Mais arrêtez de dire « le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ». Les paroles de chacun deviendront pour lui un lourd fardeau. Vous avez déformé les paroles du Dieu vivant, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, notre Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini "mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}" hamtautaja tena, kwa maana mzigo utakuwa kwa kila mtu neno lake mwenyewe; nanyi mmeyapotosha maneno ya Mungu aliye hai, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wetu.
sw.B: Lakini kamwe msiseme tena "mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," kwa sababu neno la kila mtu mwenyewe litakuwa mzigo wake, nanyi mnayapotosha maneno ya Mungu aliye hai, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wetu.
sw.R: Lakini acheni kusema "mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Maneno ya kila mtu mwenyewe yatakuwa mzigo mzito kwake. Mmeyapotosha maneno ya Mungu aliye hai, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wetu.

vi.L: Nhưng "gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}" các ngươi không được nhắc đến nữa, vì gánh nặng của mỗi người sẽ là chính lời của người ấy; và các ngươi đã bóp méo lời của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta.
vi.B: Nhưng các ngươi đừng bao giờ nói đến "gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}" nữa, vì lời nói của mỗi người sẽ trở thành gánh nặng cho chính người ấy, và các ngươi đã bóp méo lời của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta.
vi.R: Nhưng các ngươi phải thôi nói "gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}." Chính lời nói của mỗi người sẽ trở thành gánh nặng đè trên người ấy. Các ngươi đã bóp méo lời của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của chúng ta.

ko.L: 그러나 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐"을 너희는 다시 입에 올리지 마라. 저마다 자기의 말이 자기에게 짐이 될 것이다. 너희가 살아 계신 하나님, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 우리 하나님의 말씀을 왜곡했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐"이라는 말은 다시는 입에 올리지 마라. 각 사람이 하는 말이 그 사람에게 짐이 될 것이다. 너희는 살아 계신 하나님, 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 우리 하나님의 말씀을 왜곡하고 있다.
ko.R: 그러나 너희는 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐"이라는 말을 더 이상 하지 마라. 각 사람이 하는 말이 그 사람에게 무거운 짐이 될 것이다. 너희는 살아 계신 하나님, 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 우리 하나님의 말씀을 비틀어 버렸다.

pt.L: Mas "o fardo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}" vocês não mencionarão mais, pois o fardo será para cada um a sua própria palavra; e vocês distorceram as palavras do Deus vivo, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o nosso Deus.
pt.B: Mas vocês nunca mais devem falar do "fardo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}", porque a própria palavra de cada um se tornará o seu fardo, e vocês distorcem as palavras do Deus vivo, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o nosso Deus.
pt.R: Mas vocês têm de parar de dizer "o fardo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}". As próprias palavras de cada um vão se tornar um fardo pesado para ele. Vocês distorceram as palavras do Deus vivo, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o nosso Deus.

decisions.choice: the burden will be to each one their own word: their own words will weigh on them
alternatives: each one's own word is his oracle
decisions.reason: The words can be read in two ways: each person's own word becomes his "burden", the load that crushes him; or each one calls his own word a "burden", passing off his own ideas as a message from God. The first fits the play of verse 33. The rendering keeps the Hebrew's openness at Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the first reading.

decisions.choice: the living God: the God who acts, unlike lifeless idols
decisions.reason: God is called "the living God" in contrast with idols (10:10). The prophets twist the words of the one God who is truly alive.

decisions.choice: Each person's own words will become a heavy burden for them
decisions.reason: Readable follows the first reading in m1.

decisions.choice: "살아 계신 하나님 ... 우리 하나님", with the honorific
decisions.reason: "Our God" shows that the prophet speaks here of God, so the title takes "계신" and Readable "거느리신", as the terms note does when the prophet speaks about God.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־הַנָּבִ֑יא מֶה־עָנָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה וּמַה־דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus you will say to the prophet: what has answered you Yahweh? and what has spoken Yahweh?

en.L: Thus you will say to the prophet, "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered you?" and "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken?"
en.B: This is how you are to speak to a prophet: "What answer has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} given you?" or "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said?"
en.R: When you speak to a prophet, ask, "What answer did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you?" or "What did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say?"

es.L: Así dirás al profeta: «¿Qué te ha respondido {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?», y «¿Qué ha hablado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».
es.B: Así es como debes hablarle a un profeta: «¿Qué respuesta te ha dado {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?», o «¿Qué ha dicho {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».
es.R: Cuando hables con un profeta, pregúntale: «¿Qué respuesta te dio {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?», o «¿Qué dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}?».

fr.L: Ainsi tu diras au prophète : « Que t’a répondu {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? » et « Qu’a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? »
fr.B: Voici comment tu parleras à un prophète : « Quelle réponse {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a-t-il donnée ? » ou « Qu’a dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? »
fr.R: Quand tu parles à un prophète, demande-lui : « Quelle réponse {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a-t-il donnée ? » ou « Qu’est-ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit ? »

sw.L: Hivi ndivyo utakavyomwambia nabii, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekujibu nini?" na "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nini?"
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo utakavyozungumza na nabii: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekupa jibu gani?" au "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nini?"
sw.R: Unapozungumza na nabii, uliza, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikupa jibu gani?" au "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema nini?"

vi.L: Ngươi hãy nói với nhà tiên tri như vầy: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trả lời ông gì?" và "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán gì?"
vi.B: Đây là cách các ngươi phải nói với một nhà tiên tri: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trả lời ông thế nào?" hoặc "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán gì?"
vi.R: Khi nói với một nhà tiên tri, các ngươi hãy hỏi: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã trả lời ông thế nào?" hoặc "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán gì?"

ko.L: 너는 예언자에게 이와 같이 말하여라. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 무엇이라고 대답하셨느냐?" "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 무엇이라고 말씀하셨느냐?"
ko.B: 너희는 예언자에게 이렇게 말하여라. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 어떤 대답을 주셨느냐?" "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 무엇이라고 말씀하셨느냐?"
ko.R: 너희가 예언자에게 말할 때에는 이렇게 물어라. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 어떤 대답을 주셨느냐?" "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 무엇이라고 말씀하셨느냐?"

pt.L: Assim dirás ao profeta: "Que te respondeu {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}?" e "Que falou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}?"
pt.B: É assim que cada um deve falar a um profeta: "Que resposta {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te deu?" ou "O que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse?"
pt.R: Quando alguém falar com um profeta, pergunte: "Que resposta {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} te deu?" ou "O que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse?"

decisions.choice: you will say ... answered you: each person speaking to a prophet
decisions.reason: "You will say" is singular here: each person is to put the question this way. The ending on "answered you" is unusual in form, but it plainly refers to the prophet being asked.

decisions.choice: the prophet: any prophet
decisions.reason: The question is for any prophet, true or false. A true one can answer it.

decisions.choice: "ông" for the prophet in the people's question
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" here is each person speaking; Literal keeps the singular "ngươi" for the one who asks, as the Hebrew, and Balanced and Readable use "các ngươi" for all of them. The prophet is addressed with the respectful "ông".

decisions.choice: dirás (L); cada um deve (B); alguém ... pergunte (R); te (to a prophet)
decisions.reason: "You will say" is singular here (m1): each person is to ask in this way. Literal keeps the singular "dirás"; Balanced and Readable say "cada um", "alguém", so that the reader does not take it as said to Jeremiah. The question to the prophet uses "te", as people ask a prophet about God's word in the words of the Hebrew; a reader may expect "você".

source.text: וְאִם־מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָה֮ תֹּאמֵרוּ֒ לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה יַ֧עַן אֲמָרְכֶ֛ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאמְר֖וּ מַשָּׂ֥א יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And if [the] burden of Yahweh you say, therefore thus says Yahweh: because you have said this word, [the] burden of Yahweh, and I sent to you, saying, not you shall say, [the] burden of Yahweh,

en.L: But if you say, "The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Because you have said this word, "The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," though I sent to you, saying, "You shall not say, 'The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},'"
en.B: But if you do say, "{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Because you have used these words, "{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," even though I sent word to you and said, "Do not say, '{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden,'"
en.R: But suppose you keep saying "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." Then this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I sent you a message telling you not to say "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." But you have said it anyway.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}», por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Porque {{plural_you:han dicho|habéis dicho}} esta palabra, «La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}», aunque yo {{plural_you:les|os}} envié a decir: «No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: “La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”»,
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}», entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Porque {{plural_you:han usado|habéis usado}} estas palabras, «La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}», aunque yo {{plural_you:les|os}} mandé decir: «No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: “La carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”»,
es.R: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} diciendo «la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}». Entonces esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} mandé un mensaje {{plural_you:diciéndoles|diciéndoos}} que no {{plural_you:dijeran|dijerais}} «la carga {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}». Pero {{plural_you:ustedes lo han|vosotros lo habéis}} dicho de todos modos.

fr.L: Mais si vous dites : « Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », alors ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Parce que vous avez dit cette parole : « Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », alors que je vous ai envoyé dire : « Vous ne direz pas : “Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}” »,
fr.B: Mais si vous dites quand même : « Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Parce que vous avez employé ces mots : « Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} », alors que je vous avais fait dire : « Ne dites pas : “Le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}” »,
fr.R: Mais supposons que vous continuiez à dire « le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ». Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je vous ai envoyé un message pour vous dire de ne pas dire « le fardeau {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ». Mais vous l’avez dit quand même.

sw.L: Lakini mkisema, "Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Kwa sababu mmesema neno hili, "Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," ingawa niliwatumia ujumbe, kusema, "Msiseme, 'Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},'"
sw.B: Lakini mkisema kweli, "Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," basi hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Kwa sababu mmetumia maneno haya, "Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}," ingawa niliwatumia ujumbe nikasema, "Msiseme, 'Mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}},'"
sw.R: Lakini tuseme mnaendelea kusema "mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Basi hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Niliwatumia ujumbe kuwaambia msiseme "mzigo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Lakini mmesema hivyo tu.

vi.L: Nhưng nếu các ngươi nói: "Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}," thì vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Vì các ngươi đã nói lời này: "Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}," dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai người đến bảo các ngươi rằng: "Các ngươi không được nói: 'Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}},'"
vi.B: Nhưng nếu các ngươi vẫn nói: "Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}," thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Vì các ngươi đã dùng những lời này: "Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}," dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai người đến bảo các ngươi: "Đừng nói: 'Gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}},'"
vi.R: Nhưng giả sử các ngươi cứ nói "gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}." Thì đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Ta đã sai người đến bảo các ngươi đừng nói "gánh nặng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}." Nhưng các ngươi vẫn cứ nói.

ko.L: 그런데 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐" 하고 말한다면, 그러므로 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 너희에게 사람을 보내어 "'{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐' 하고 말하지 마라." 하고 일렀는데도, 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐"이라는 이 말을 했으므로,
ko.B: 그런데도 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐" 하고 말한다면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 너희에게 사람을 보내어 "'{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐'이라고 말하지 마라." 하고 일렀는데도, 너희가 "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 짐"이라는 말을 썼으므로,

decisions.choice: because: the reason for the judgment in verses 39-40
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 39: because they keep using the word after God forbade it, he will throw them off.

decisions.choice: I sent to you: God's command came through his prophet
decisions.reason: God sent the message of verses 34-36 through Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: I sent you a message ... But you have said it anyway. (new sentences)
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the reason in short sentences and begins the judgment with a new sentence in verse 39.

decisions.choice: God's earlier command placed before "you have said this word"
decisions.reason: In Korean a concessive clause ("일렀는데도") comes before the main clause, so the command is given first; the sentence still runs on into verse 39, as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: I will surely forget you (the Hebrew text)
alternatives: I will surely lift you up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will forget you". A few Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient versions have a verb that differs by one letter, "I will lift you up", the root of "burden": God would pick the people up like a load and throw it away. The Hebrew is kept. This claim about the manuscripts and versions is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: cast you away: the verb of verse 33
decisions.reason: God does to them what he warned in verse 33: he throws them down like a load.

decisions.choice: the city I gave to you and to your fathers: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was God's gift with the land (7:7, 14). Being thrown away from his presence means exile from the city and the temple (7:15).

decisions.choice: everlasting shame that will not be forgotten: the same words as 20:11
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses these words in 20:11 of his persecutors. Here they close the chapter: God will "forget" the people (verse 39), but their shame will not be forgotten.

decisions.choice: everlasting: lasting into the far future
decisions.reason: The word means a very long time, without a set end. It is the shame of the exile, remembered long after.

decisions.choice: disgrace, shame
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "disgrace" for the first word, which means scorn heaped on someone.
